transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-06-18 Start: 15:00 PT Duration: 42 min Attendees: Ella Park (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (CTO, FinEdge), Michael Rivera (ML Eng), Tom Li (Head Infra)

Summary: Quick signoff on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed go/no-go thresholds for latency, quality, and cost; agreed benchmark dataset and reporting format; clarified workload sizing (QPS, token distribution); established timeline (3-week POC) and immediate action items.

Topics: Success criteria (latency p95, quality/regression thresholds, cost per 1k tokens); Workload sizing (QPS, token lengths, peak vs steady); Benchmark plan (hosted vs dedicated, quantization profiles); Acceptance tests and reporting format (per-request CSV + dashboard metrics); Timeline and signoff process.

Transcript: [00:00] Ella: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Uh Sara, Michael, Tom, appreciate you making time. We'll run through the success criteria doc and get signoff so Jonah can start the baseline runs.
[00:14] Sara: Yeah thanks Ella. Wanted to make sure we nail the thresholds, like what counts as a pass vs fail. We have compliance folks watching so clarity is important.
[00:23] Jonah: Totally, I'll try and keep it concrete - latency, quality, cost. We'll also define the test harness and the reporting CSV fields.
[00:30] Michael: Quick note, our main workload is customer support triage + fraud flagging, so mostly ~200-600 token requests, average ~350 tokens. Peak traffic might hit 100 QPS for short bursts, steady is around 30-40 QPS.
[00:44] Tom: From infra side we need to confirm we can open the S3 bucket and allow the Redwood test runners in, and also whether Dedicated requires us to do VPC peering.
[00:52] Ella: Great context. On the doc we proposed success criteria: 1) Latency: p95 response time under 450ms for typical 350-token requests on Dedicated config; hosted target is p95 under 650ms. 2) Quality: evaluation set EM/accuracy > 85% on the golden QA set and no regressions > 3% vs baseline. 3) Cost: effective cost per 1k tokens under agreed target in spreadsheet. Do these look reasonable?
[01:20] Sara: The latency numbers seem aggressive but okay for Dedicated. For hosted we need a clear fallback plan if they exceed.
[01:27] Jonah: We'll include automated fallback policy in the test - if p95 > threshold for two consecutive runs we'll mark as degraded and capture traces. Also we'll run tests with prefix KV cache warm and cold to cover both.
[01:40] Michael: On quality, can you clarify the eval? Is it automated exact match or are we doing human review too?
[01:47] Ella: Primary is automated EM/semantic similarity on the golden 1k samples. Secondary is a human review on a 200-sample stratified set for edge cases - that's part of acceptance. If human review finds >5% false positives for fraud flags we fail.
[02:05] Tom: For the Dedicated deployment, our security team requires KMS integration and audit logs; you'll send the SOC2 docs, right?
[02:12] Jonah: Yep we'll include SOC2, the private deployment checklist, and a quick guide for KMS/HSM integration. We'll also include event-level audit log format in the reporting artifact.
[02:25] Sara: Good. For the benchmark we want both Hosted and Dedicated runs, and also an INT8 quantized run to compare cost/latency tradeoffs. Can you do that?
[02:33] Jonah: Yes - plan is: baseline hosted run (no quant), dedicated baseline (no quant), then dedicated INT8 quant run. We'll capture per-request latency, tokens, model variant, quantization flag, and success/error types.
[02:45] Ella: Reporting format: agreed we do a per-request CSV with columns: request_id, timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, model, quant_flag, error_code, em_score, similarity_score. We'll also provide an aggregated dashboard with p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/sec), cost estimate, and quality regression charts.
[03:05] Michael: That CSV looks good. For privacy we will share masked request ids and masked PII - Michael: I'll deliver the masked dataset.
[03:12] Michael: Yep I'll deliver 10k masked requests plus schema and the golden 1k eval set by Friday.
[03:18] Ella: Perfect. Acceptance tests: run 3 consecutive benchmark runs over 24 hours for each config; pass if p95 under threshold and EM>85% and no more than 3% regression. Also we'll run a soak test at 75% peak QPS for 2 hours to check stability.
[03:40] Sara: What's our go/no-go decision process? If one metric fails do we auto-fail whole POC?
[03:46] Jonah: We recommend a weighted pass/fail: latency and quality are hard stops - if either misses threshold it's a no-go. Cost is advisory but must be within 20% of target or require explicit acceptance from your finance lead. So: quality fail -> no-go; latency fail -> no-go; cost overrun -> flagged and discussed but not automatic fail.
[04:06] Tom: That seems reasonable. Also need the network diagram and IP allowlist for the test runners.
[04:12] Ella: We'll include that in the security pack.
[04:15] Sara: Timeline? You said 3 weeks earlier. Break that down?
[04:20] Jonah: Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria, get dataset, provision infra. Week 1: baseline hosted + dedicated runs, initial quant test. Week 2: soak tests, human review, follow-up runs. Week 3: final reporting and signoff. If everything passes, we do roll decision and plan Dedicated provisioning.
[04:40] Michael: Do you need any special SDK versions or runtime flags? Our infra is on k8s with g4dn instances for staging.
[04:48] Jonah: For the Dedicated benchmarking we'll provide a container and runner script; no special SDK beyond the Redwood client. For k8s staging you can run the test harness but we prefer Redwood-run benchmarks to ensure consistent environment.
[04:59] Speaker 2: um can you repeat the exact p95 numbers?
[05:02] Ella: Sure - Dedicated p95 < 450ms for 350-token average, Hosted p95 < 650ms. p50 targets are listed in the spreadsheet too but p95 is the go/no-go.
[05:12] Sara: On reporting frequency - we want daily aggregated emails during the run and the full CSV at the end.
[05:20] Jonah: We'll push the daily summary to the shared S3 path and also populate the dashboard; link in the daily email.
[05:26] Michael: About cost estimation, can you show rough per-1k token numbers?
[05:30] Ella: We'll include a range in the spreadsheet; approximate numbers depend on quantization and batching - Jonah will provide the compute-hours and cost breakdown per model variant.
[05:38] Tom: One security ask - can Redwood redact model prompts in logs or set retention? Our compliance needs 90-day retention and redaction of PII.
[05:47] Jonah: Retention and redaction are configurable; we'll set retention to 90 days for the POC and enable prompt redaction. We'll capture audit logs in immutable form for your audit team.
[05:58] Sara: Alright, happy with that. Any open blockers?
[06:02] Michael: I need the sample format for masked PII to ensure we're aligned on masking rules.
[06:08] Ella: I'll attach a sample mask spec with the benchmark template.
[06:12] Sara: Good. On acceptance - who signs off? CTO or ML lead?
[06:16] Tom: Our internal process is ML lead confirms quality, infra confirms security, and the CTO gives final signoff. So Michael -> Tom -> Sara sequentially.
[06:26] Ella: We'll capture that in the doc: signoff path Michael, Tom, Sara.
[06:30] Jonah: One more technical point - we'll run warm and cold cache scenarios and capture KV cache hit rate in the CSV as "kv_cache_hit". Note: transcription might show KV cash earlier.
[06:42] Michael: Ok, good. Lastly, what about concurrency and batching settings for the test?
[06:47] Jonah: We'll test with your steady QPS (40) with Redwood recommended batching and then a high-throughput run at 100 QPS. We'll vary batch size to show latency vs throughput tradeoffs.
[07:00] Sara: That covers most. Let's confirm deliverables and dates quickly.
[07:06] Ella: Deliverables: final success criteria doc (Ella) by 2025-06-19; sample dataset (Michael) by 2025-06-20; SOC2 + security pack (Redwood) by 2025-06-19; baseline runs (Jonah) week of 2025-06-23; final report and signoff end of week of 2025-07-07.
[07:26] Tom: I'll get the network allowlist to you by 2025-06-21.
[07:30] Sara: If we pass, what's the next step operationally?
[07:33] Ella: If POC passes, we move to capacity planning for Dedicated, contract/commit discussion, and production rollout plan.
[07:40] Michael: Fine. I'm good to proceed.
[07:43] Ella: Great - thanks everyone. We'll send the doc and spreadsheet shortly.
[07:47] Jonah: I'll queue the baseline runner once we have the sample dataset.
[07:51] Sara: Thanks all. End of call.

Attachments/Links noted in-chat: Success criteria spreadsheet (will be shared); Benchmark template CSV (will be shared); SOC2 + security pack (will be shared); S3 path for results: s3://finedge-redwood-poc/results (placeholder).

Acceptance summary: Quality: Golden eval EM/accuracy >= 85% and no regression > 3% -> PASS/FAIL (hard stop); Latency: p95 <= 450ms (Dedicated) / <=650ms (Hosted) -> PASS/FAIL (hard stop); Cost: cost per 1k tokens within 20% of target -> advisory; Stability: soak test at 75% peak QPS for 2 hours with no critical errors -> PASS/FAIL; Human review: stratified 200-sample human review with false positive rate for fraud flags <=5% -> PASS/FAIL.

POC timeline: 2025-06-19: Success criteria + SOC2/security pack delivered by Redwood; 2025-06-20: FinEdge provides masked 10k sample + golden 1k eval set; Week of 2025-06-23: Baseline runs (hosted + dedicated) and INT8 quant test; Week of 2025-06-30: Soak tests and human review; Week of 2025-07-07: Final report and signoff.

Notes on reporting format: per-request CSV columns: request_id, timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, model, quant_flag, error_code, em_score, similarity_score; plus aggregated dashboard with p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost estimate, quality charts. Daily summary emails during run and full CSV at end.

Action items recap: Ella: Send final success criteria + benchmark spreadsheet by 2025-06-19; Michael: Provide masked dataset + schema by 2025-06-20; Jonah: Baseline runs and cost/latency spreadsheet (week of 2025-06-23); Tom: Network allowlist and confirm VPC requirements by 2025-06-21.
